title: The Man Who Sold The Eiffel Tower Twice
sources: Smithsonian Magazine, 'The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower' by Robert K. Massie (Victor Lustig, 1925: invited six scrap dealers to a secret meeting at the Hotel de Crillon, claimed the city would scrap the tower quietly; one paid a bribe + 20,000 francs; Lustig fled to Vienna; the dealer was too embarrassed to report it)

FBI Historical File, 'Count Victor Lustig' (Lustig returned to Paris six months later, sold the tower again to a different dealer; this time police were waiting but Lustig talked his way out and escaped)
Paris Police Archives, 1925-1926 (confirms two separate scrap-dealer frauds involving the Eiffel Tower; neither sale was official; the tower was never slated for demolition)

lines.text: Paris, 1925. The Eiffel Tower was supposed to be temporary.
A smooth talker named Victor Lustig read that and saw a payday.
He invited six scrap dealers to a secret meeting at a fancy hotel.
Told them the city wanted the tower gone hush hush and he was the man to sell it.
One dealer bit. Paid a bribe on top of the price twenty thousand francs.
Lustig took the money and vanished to Vienna.
But the dealer was too embarrassed to tell the police he had bought a landmark.
So six months later Lustig came back and did it again.
Second dealer paid. This time the cops were waiting.
Lustig talked his way out again but the tower never went anywhere.
